sampling_model.design: A triangular array of binary sequential experiments with fixed finite-population potential outcomes and assignment as the only randomness.
sampling_model.treatment: Given \(\mathcal F_{n,t-1}\), \(A_{nt}\) is Bernoulli with known logged predictable probability \(e_{nt}\).
sampling_model.overlap: The rare-arm probability follows \(t e_{nt}\approx \bar q(t/n)\) after an early cutoff, with bounded cumulative hazard and \(0<e_{nt}\le\rho<1\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Predictable regressions \(m_{nt}(a)\) may be arbitrary within their bound; their treated residuals follow a deterministic Lipschitz profile on one common high-probability event.
sampling_model.randomness: Only the known adaptive randomization law is random; there is no superpopulation sampling assumption.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Definition 1 permits general positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, while Theorem 4(ii)'s Gaussian AIPW conclusion requires Condition 3, including its negligible-maximum part (ii).
Theorem 1 constructs doubly robust betting confidence sequences under predictable logging.
Proposition 1 proves selective type-I error control for the selective randomization p-value.
Theorem 1 proves asymptotic type-I error control for simulation with optimism in specified adaptive designs.
Proposition 2 gives an exact compound-Poisson law for an HT rate estimator under independent Poisson importance sampling.
Finite-population limited-overlap estimators are asymptotically Gaussian when their effective sample size diverges.
Any valid i.i.d. bounded-mean confidence interval obeys an inverse-information-projection width lower bound.
Stein perturbation yields explicit total-variation compound-Poisson approximation bounds for integer-valued sums.
Weighted Bernoulli and Poisson sums admit generalized Dickman approximation bounds.
Theorem 1 gives a semiparametrically efficient Gaussian limit for the truncated A2IPW estimator.
Resampling simulations find tighter superior-arm and wider inferior-arm intervals under real-time adaptive randomization.

body.tldr: At the critical rare-arm boundary, the finite-population AIPW error need not be Gaussian. On this note's structured binary profile subclass, a stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer and directed-rational convolution give a computable atom-safe confidence interval with uniform randomization coverage and explicit oracle slack. Separately, the pointwise-minimal admissible intensity \(\bar q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) and the capped clipped residual jointly optimize the all-confidence-set late-void converse: at \(0<d<d_{\max}\), honesty forces limiting large-diameter probability at least \([\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha]_+\). The intensity elbow \(d_q=d(1-c/(2L_q))\), when \(L_q>c/2\), coexists in either order with the interior residual elbow \(M^2/L_r\). Exact attainment remains confined to each selected two-sign subexperiment, and subclass inclusion transfers only the converse to Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive class. The original linear-ramp frontier, the exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) result, the directed \(13/32\) certificate, and the high-hazard \(0.442M\) radius remain unchanged.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive-design class permits positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, but their Gaussian AIPW theorem requires a negligible-maximum condition that fails at bounded cumulative hazard. Existing adaptive and i.i.d. width results neither calibrate the signed atomic compound-Poisson law nor optimize the complete-log common-void obstruction jointly over the declared intensity class \(\mathcal Q\) and the simultaneous \(M\)-bounded, \(L_r\)-Lipschitz residual constraints.
project_justification.niche: The boundary has two distinct deliverables. Structured deterministic profiles permit computable atom-safe positive calibration. For all-estimator information limits, \(\bar q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) is the pointwise-smallest admissible intensity and the capped clipped ramp saturates \(\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}\); together they produce a joint late-void probability--diameter envelope with separate intensity and residual elbows.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the finite adaptive-to-Poisson transfer and profile-net interval theorem on the declared structured subclass, plus an exact finite-sample tradeoff for each intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair and the jointly optimized asymptotic envelope \([\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha]_+\). A sourced subclass-inclusion argument lifts only that converse to Li and Zhao's larger baseline binary adaptive class. Pairwise attainment, positive calibration, the original linear frontier, the exact ramp certificate, and the high-hazard radius retain their separately stated scopes.

body.related_work: Li and Zhao (2026) provide the closest design-based setup: fixed finite-population potential outcomes, positive assignment probabilities that may be prespecified functions of history, and predictable AIPW regression. Their baseline binary class contains the deterministic intensity-optimized clipped ramps, but their Theorem 4(ii) assumes Condition 3; these bounded-hazard witnesses fail its negligible-maximum part because late standardized increments remain nonnegligible. The present joint intensity-and-residual converse therefore transfers by subclass inclusion, while its matching confidence-set construction remains sharp only inside each selected two-sign subexperiment and the positive profile-net theorem remains confined to this note's structured subclass. Bibaut and Kallus (2025) organize adaptive inference into Gaussian repair, always-valid methods, and direct inversion of nonnormal laws. Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) provide predictable-logging confidence sequences, Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026) study selection-conditioned randomization tests, and Cho, Bibaut, and Kallus (2025) invert simulated adaptive laws; none supplies this finite-population signed atomic calibration or the jointly optimized common-void envelope. Chen et al. (2026) obtain a compound-Poisson HT law under independent Poisson importance sampling, while Hong, Leung, and Li (2020) treat limited overlap with diverging effective information. Shekhar and Ramdas (2023) prove i.i.d. bounded-mean width bounds rather than the present exact sequential two-sign tradeoff. Barbour and Xia (1999) support compound-Poisson error accounting, and Bhattacharjee and Goldstein (2019) identify the generalized Dickman constant-profile reduction. Liberali et al. (2025) remain the applied consumer, conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge for GUSTO-1 and EUROPA.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-transfer theorem couples the AIPW statistic, not the complete experiments, and therefore does not imply the all-estimator lower bound. The joint frontier instead uses an exact common subprobability on a late-arm void event. Its intensity certificate is pointwise optimal only for deterministic designs of the stated form generated from \(q\in\mathcal Q\), and its residual certificate is optimal only within the declared late-void two-sign witness geometry under the existing \(M,L_r\) constraints. The matching procedure knows the selected pair, so it establishes no global minimax attainment over the full structured class. Subclass inclusion transfers the converse, but neither attainment nor positive calibration, to Li and Zhao's baseline class. The positive theorem still requires fixed profiles, deterministic domination for same-log threshold selection, and supplied profile and early-variation contracts. The \(0.442M\) high-hazard result remains a subfamily upper bound. The polynomial bit-complexity question remains open because the pruning invariant gives no polynomial bound on the number of profile boxes straddling the certification boundary.
body.honest_scope: Uniform finite-experiment coverage applies to the declared bounded Lipschitz intensity and signed-residual profile subclass with its supplied common profile event, early quadratic-variation envelope, and certified inputs. The all-confidence-set envelope \([\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha]_+\) is jointly optimized among deterministic \(q\in\mathcal Q\) late-void designs and two-sign residual witnesses under the stated \(M,L_r\) constraints. Exact attainment is only for each selected two-sign intensity-optimized clipped-ramp subexperiment; no global minimax attainment is claimed for the structured class or Li and Zhao's larger baseline class. Only the converse transfers to that baseline class by subclass inclusion. The positive profile-net theorem, the original linear-ramp frontier, the exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) diagnostic, the directed \(13/32\) certificate, and the \(0.442M\) high-hazard result keep their prior scopes. The polynomial certificate OEQ remains open with its existing boundary-straddling pruning obstruction; no complexity exponent is asserted.
